source.title: Rank-Transformed Dissimilarity Profiles for High-Dimensional Classification

algorithm_steps.description: Construct a pairwise dissimilarity matrix among the training observations using a chosen metric (e.g., Euclidean).
algorithm_steps.source_span: Section 2.2: construct a pairwise dissimilarity matrix among the training observations

algorithm_steps.description: Summarize each training observation by its class-wise dissimilarity profile. For an observation in class i, compute the vector of mean dissimilarities to all classes j=1..k.
algorithm_steps.source_span: Section 2.2: summarize each observation by its class-wise dissimilarity profile

algorithm_steps.description: For a new observation W, compute its class-wise dissimilarity profile by calculating its mean dissimilarity to each of the k classes in the training set.
algorithm_steps.source_span: Section 2.2: compute the corresponding class-wise dissimilarity profile for a new observation

algorithm_steps.description: Apply a rank transformation to the dissimilarity profiles. Convert the dissimilarity values into ranks within each class dimension to improve robustness.
algorithm_steps.source_span: Abstract: introduce a rank-transformed algorithm that converts dissimilarities into class-wise rank profiles

algorithm_steps.description: Classify the new observation in the resulting low-dimensional rank profile space using a standard low-dimensional classifier (e.g., Quadratic Discriminant Analysis).
algorithm_steps.source_span: Abstract: yielding a compact representation for classification... Section 2.2: classify the new observation in the resulting low-dimensional profile space

assumptions.name: independent_observations
assumptions.source_span: Section 2.2: The observations are assumed independent

assumptions.name: labeled_training_data
assumptions.description: Availability of a labeled training set S with observations Z and class labels g.
assumptions.source_span: Section 2.2: Let S = {(Z_i, g_i): i in [N]} be a labeled training set

assumptions.name: high_dimensional_geometry_signal
assumptions.description: High-dimensional geometry induces systematic within-class and between-class dissimilarity patterns under distributional changes (location, scale, etc.).
assumptions.source_span: Abstract: high-dimensional geometry can induce systematic within-class and between-class dissimilarity patterns

data_requirements: Labeled training set with features Z in R^d and class labels g in {1,...,k}
New observation W in R^d for prediction
Choice of dissimilarity metric appropriate for data type (e.g., Euclidean for vectors)

mathematical_specification.decision_rule: Assign W to the class predicted by the low-dimensional classifier (e.g., QDA) applied to the rank-transformed dissimilarity profile of W.
parameters: class-wise mean dissimilarities for training observations
tuning_parameters: choice of low-dimensional classifier (e.g., QDA parameters)
mathematical_specification.estimator: Class-wise dissimilarity profile: For observation i in class i, profile D_i = (D_{i1}, D_{i2}, ..., D_{ik}) where D_{ij} is the mean dissimilarity between observation i and all observations in class j.

implementation_components.description: Calculate class-wise dissimilarity profiles for training observations.

implementation_invariants.name: rank_transformation_required
implementation_invariants.rationale: The method explicitly relies on rank transformation for robustness, distinguishing it from standard dissimilarity profiling.

implementation_invariants.name: class_wise_profile_dimension
implementation_invariants.rationale: The profile dimension must equal the number of classes k, not the original feature dimension d.

warnings: The text mentions 'standard low-dimensional methods such as quadratic discriminant analysis' but does not provide the full mathematical derivation of the QDA step. The implementation assumes QDA or similar is used.
The choice of dissimilarity metric is flexible (Euclidean, Manhattan, etc.) and not fixed by the text. The implementation must allow this to be specified.
The text does not specify the exact method for handling ties in rank transformation.
